properties.statement: [BL-148] A session's tool surface changed under it mid-conversation and nothing said so — the BL-32 hazard running in reverse
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by an /adopt pass over music_graph, a ~11k-LOC Python research repo taken from an empty graph to 134 nodes / 379 edges. Reported in that project's own reflow2_feedback.txt.* When the shared server restarted it came back on a newer binary: two tools that had not existed appeared (calibrated_against, set_evidence_scope \u2014 the [BL-106]/[BL-126]/[BL-136] family, merged that morning) and served_by.binary_mtime_unix jumped from 1785556181 to 1785561997. This is the [BL-32] hazard inverted \u2014 not a stale server serving an old surface, but a live session whose surface changed underneath it. Nothing broke, and the version string stayed 0.20.0, so version alone would not have revealed it. served_by.binary_mtime_unix is what made it visible, which is an argument for keeping that field. Fix shape, and the reporter's own: a one-line note in the tool result when the surface changes mid-session \u2014 *\"server restarted on a newer build; N tools added\"* \u2014 turning something noticed by accident into something a session is told. Related to [BL-113] and the launch-wrapper trap from the other direction: that one is a session talking to the wrong design for hours, this is a session talking to a different *surface* than the one it started with. Both are silent, and both are only findable by inspecting the process rather than the protocol. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-148 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
